Interesting: the `MainBuilder` visit_String emits `char var1[maxsize+1]` and reserves IDs for each char. visit_Array reserves an ID for the array itself then each element. visit_Struct reserves an ID for the struct, then fields. visit_Alias reserves no ID and delegates to the target type. This matches the PROTOCOL description:
- inputs in parameter order, then non-void result, start at x0
- each visited bool, char, int, enum, string buffer, array, struct reserves one increasing xN
- scalar has one object; composite itself has no object, then children in order reserve IDs recursively
- String(N) has N char objects after its buffer ID
- alias reserves no ID and adds no path component
- Even zero-length composites reserve their own ID. Void reserves none.
